whyThisMatters: Real payroll and recruitment decisions are fast — a form arrives, a deadline looms, and you don't always get time to research whether it's genuine. This game trains your reflex for good habits, and helps you catch things that only sound safe.
rememberThis: This month's habit to carry forward: fast instinct is good, but some things only sound safe — a familiar agent name, an urgent deadline, a portal migration notice. When you are not sure, slow down and check before you trust the label.

discussionPrompts: Ask the group which bubble tricked them. Most people get at least one of the trick bubbles wrong on their first try.
Ask why recognising an agent's name isn't the same as checking their domain.
Ask why checking despite a tight candidate deadline is included as a trick bubble here — it's not wrong, it's just the one people most often skip.
facilitatorNotes.commonWrongAnswer: The most common mistake is tapping anything that sounds familiar — a recognisable agent name, an urgent recruitment deadline, a portal-migration notice — without checking the exact domain or process behind it. The trick bubbles are there to catch that habit.

bubbles.text: Check the sender's email domain
bubbles.why: Look-alike domains are how fraudsters pose as staff, agents and candidates.

bubbles.text: Confirm bank changes in the portal
bubbles.why: The portal checks identity, so fake bank-change requests are caught.

bubbles.text: Report suspicious attachments
bubbles.why: Reporting lets security remove the malicious file before anyone opens it.

bubbles.text: Confirm candidates via a known agent
bubbles.why: Checking with a trusted agent exposes impostors posing as job candidates.

bubbles.text: Use the crew portal for bank updates
bubbles.why: The portal verifies identity, so payroll can't be redirected by a fake email.

bubbles.text: Check an attachment's file type
bubbles.why: Files disguised as documents can hide programs that infect your computer.

bubbles.text: Call back on a known HR number
bubbles.why: A saved number reaches the real person, not whoever sent the message.

bubbles.text: Flag a mismatched email domain
bubbles.why: A domain that doesn't match the sender's company often means a phishing attempt.

bubbles.text: Hold reference forms until verified
bubbles.why: Fake reference forms can carry malware or steal a candidate's details.

bubbles.text: Escalate unusual payroll requests
bubbles.why: Payroll fraud relies on one person acting quickly; escalating stops it.

bubbles.text: Click Enable Content on a file
bubbles.why: Enabling content lets hidden macros run and install malware on your PC.

bubbles.text: Email bank details in reply
bubbles.why: Replies can reach a scammer and expose bank details used in payroll fraud.

bubbles.text: Skip checks because of a deadline
bubbles.why: Scammers invent deadlines so you skip the checks that would expose them.

bubbles.text: Tap a link in a payroll text
bubbles.why: Fake payroll texts lead to sites that steal your login or bank details.

bubbles.text: Ignore a mismatched email domain
bubbles.why: A domain that doesn't match is a classic sign the sender is an impostor.

bubbles.text: Share candidate data unverified
bubbles.why: Personal data sent to an impostor can be used for identity theft.

bubbles.text: Trust an urgent recruitment request
bubbles.why: Urgent hiring requests are a common pretext for stealing data or money.

bubbles.text: Enable macros on a reference form
bubbles.why: Macros in a document can quietly install malware once you enable them.

bubbles.text: Change bank details on an email alone
bubbles.why: Emails are easily faked, so fraudsters use them to redirect salary payments.

bubbles.text: Skip the standard HR process
bubbles.why: The process exists to catch fraud; skipping it removes your protection.

bubbles.text: Verify an agent whose name you know
bubbles.why: A familiar name is easily copied; it doesn't prove the message is real.

bubbles.text: Verify even when a start date is near
bubbles.why: Rushing a new starter is a pressure tactic, so checking anyway protects you.

bubbles.text: Call the number given in a text
bubbles.why: The number in a scam text connects you to the scammer, not the real company.

bubbles.text: Believe a portal move notice
bubbles.why: Fake 'portal migration' notices are used to steal staff logins.
